audit_result.proof_trace: The guard on L16 uses `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'`, which evaluates to `true` when NODE_ENV is undefined (undefined !== 'production' === true), causing err.message to be included in the HTTP 500 response. No code-level default is assigned for NODE_ENV; the ecosystem.config.json PM2 default and .env.example are deployment-specific and do not protect direct-execution scenarios.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An attacker triggers any unhandled exception (DB error, type error, malformed body) against a deployment running without NODE_ENV set (e.g., direct `node dist/index.js` without PM2 or .env loaded); the HTTP 500 response body includes the `details` field containing the raw err.message, leaking internal error information.

PROP-stem-bot-v21-inv-022.text: NODE_ENV must default to production-safe behavior when undefined (no error detail leakage).
PROP-stem-bot-v21-inv-022.assertion: NODE_ENV == undefined => error_response behaves as NODE_ENV == 'production'
